correctness.rationale: The ratios are exactly b^(-|c_i|/s), with positive code lengths because the maps are contractions. Kraft equality and strong separation give dimension s. A de Bruijn digit cycle has b^k distinct length-k blocks. Parsing at every residue defines a finite self-map; on any directed cycle its positive total digit length is a multiple of b^k, and individual advances are at most L. A shorter symbol period would induce a digit period divisible by b^k and thus an earlier return to the same parser residue. At distinct parser residues a common symbol prefix encodes at most k-1 digits. Applying its similarity to distinct first-level pieces gives the stated gap. The resulting cardinalities tend to infinity, exactly as required by the critical-content definition, and the normalized gap is at least (b/L)δ^s. The unequal-ratio example has separated invariant interval images, with minimum interval gap 3/16.
residual_risks: The finite replay is corroboration only and sampled only single-winding cycles; the proof does not assume single winding.

value.rationale: At the critical exponent, dimension equality permits every large-period normalized gap to shrink to zero. This result rules that out quantitatively for a structurally defined, genuinely inhomogeneous class. The bound gives explicit data for constructing large separated orbits, and the parser-cycle argument works for arbitrarily many length levels. Its value is as a constructive partial answer, not as a solution for all uneven ratios.
residual_risks: No optimality of the lower bound or extension outside the exact code-derived ratio class is established.
